import importlib.util, shutil
for name in ('pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','pymupdf','PIL'):
    print(name, bool(importlib.util.find_spec(name)))
for name in ('python3','gs','pdftotext','pdftoppm','pdfinfo'):
    print(name, shutil.which(name))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
reader=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(reader.pages))
print('METADATA',reader.metadata)
parts=[]
for i,page in enumerate(reader.pages):
    parts.append(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i+1} =====\\n\\n'+page.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout'))
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(parts))
print(''.join(parts)[:33000])
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('tmp/pdfs')
for i in range(1,17):
    (p/f'page-{i:02d}.png').unlink(missing_ok=True)
(p/'manuscript.txt').unlink(missing_ok=True)
p.rmdir()
Path('tmp').rmdir()
PY"

strengths: QuEST addresses an important deployment problem with a practical approach: selectively fine-tuning time-embedding and attention-related layers using supervision from a full-precision model, without requiring original training images.

The low-bit LSUN improvements are substantial. Table 3 reports W4A4 FID reductions from EfficientDM’s 10.60 to 5.64 on Bedrooms and from 14.34 to 11.76 on Churches. The Stable Diffusion examples also demonstrate recognizable generation where the reported Q-Diffusion baseline fails.

Evaluation covers three generation tasks and four models, generally using 50,000 generated images for LDM metrics. Activation-distribution visualizations, sensitivity experiments, and component ablations provide useful empirical motivation.

Table 7 demonstrates a meaningful calibration-time improvement: 15.25 versus 23.08 GPU hours for Q-Diffusion, using the same calibration-set size while improving FID. Dataset and baseline attribution, a code link, and discussion of possible effects on watermarking and safety checking are positive aspects.
weaknesses: The theoretical justification is unsound as written. For the stated MSE loss, Taylor expansion with respect to the final output is exactly quadratic regardless of perturbation magnitude; large perturbations therefore do not establish the claimed breakdown in Section 2.3.1. Appendix B also does not justify replacing the epsilon-based quadratic term in Equation 10 with the output-residual term in Equation 5. Neither the derivation nor its assumptions establish the claimed sufficiency of selective fine-tuning.

The distinctive contribution is insufficiently isolated experimentally. EfficientDM already provides efficient quantization-aware fine-tuning, and Appendix A acknowledges prior timestep grouping. Table 7 lacks comparisons against equally sized alternative layer subsets and simultaneous versus progressive optimization. The main component ablation uses W4A8 Bedrooms, leaving the causes of the headline W4A4 improvements less well established.

The results support a narrower superiority claim. On ImageNet W4A4, QuEST has worse sFID than EfficientDM (7.93 versus 7.75) and substantially lower IS (202.45 versus 250.90). Its better FID does not resolve this concern, especially because the manuscript itself questions FID’s validity in this setting. These results require a clearer account of the quality tradeoff.

The Stable Diffusion evidence is limited to CLIPScore on 10,000 COCO prompts and qualitative examples for two prompts. CLIPScore alone does not establish visual fidelity or diversity, and the W4A4 examples show visible degradation. An image-quality evaluation and comparison with the closest fine-tuning approach would strengthen this central contribution.

The efficiency and precision claims need qualification. Section 1 retains 8-bit boundary layers and attention matrix multiplications, while Appendix A restricts quantization to the UNet, making 'full W4A4 Stable Diffusion' imprecise. No actual low-bit inference latency is reported. Table 7 also shows higher calibration memory than Q-Diffusion (12,450 versus 10,334 MB), and provides no efficiency comparison with EfficientDM.

Reproducibility from the manuscript is incomplete despite the code link: quantizer initialization and granularity, gradients through rounding, batch sizes, and exact optimization-stage schedules are insufficiently specified. These details matter for reproducing the reported low-bit accuracy and training cost.
